transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tomas Rivera (Redwood CSM); Sarah Liu (MeridianAI Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (CTO), Jamie Park (Infra), Nina Alvarez (Product)

Auto-summary (auto): MeridianAI is evaluating migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated (or Private) due to cost and data residency concerns. Key asks: parity with current evals, latency targets for chat product (p95 < 300ms for short prompts), throughput of ~50k reqs/day with peaks; compatibility with existing OpenAI API calls and fine-tuned behavior implemented via TGI/vLLM pipelines. Security: SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS. Next steps agreed: pricing, perf benchmarks, security docs, follow-up SE deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. We've also got Priya our SE and Tomas from CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Sarah: Good thanks, uh a bit short on time so appreciate the tight agenda.
[00:08] Alex: Totally, we'll keep it focused. Quick round: can each of you say role?
[00:12] Sarah: Sarah Liu, Head of ML at MeridianAI. We own inference and model ops.
[00:16] Carlos: Carlos Mendes, CTO. I'm here for infra and procurement touchpoints.
[00:20] Jamie: Jamie Park, infra engineer, I'll be the one doing the lift and shift.
[00:23] Nina: Nina Alvarez, product, here to understand risk and timelines.
[00:26] Alex: Awesome. So high level, we heard you're currently on OpenAI hosted endpoints and exploring a move to Dedicated or Private. Can you walk us through drivers and constraints?
[00:35] Sarah: Yeah, main drivers are cost at scale and data residency. We're seeing big token volumes for chat and reranking. Second, we need stronger audit logs and KMS control. Third is performance — some of our internal SLAs for short prompts need lower p95.
[00:45] Priya: And are you also running any self-hosted stacks today, like vLLM or TGI?
[00:49] Sarah: We have a small vLLM cluster for experimentation and some TGI-based pipelines for fine-tuning legacy models. But production is OpenAI. We want parity — our eval suites must pass on Redwood models/variants before we flip.
[01:00] Alex: Great — that's very common. Two threads we'll need to cover: 1) API compatibility and migration effort for your call patterns (OpenAI APIs, embeddings, chat + function calls), and 2) performance and quality parity vs your current models.
[01:12] Carlos: On compatibility, our engineers are worried about subtle differences — tokenization, output formatting, and scoring differences in rerank. How do you approach eval parity?
[01:20] Priya: We typically run a lift-and-compare: same prompt set and scoring harness run across your baseline model (OpenAI) and Redwood-hosted model variants. We instrument differences and produce a delta report by utterance and evaluation metric. We also test business-critical prompts as golden sets. Sometimes we recommend small prompt tweaks or model variant pinning.
[01:36] Sarah: OK, and on the infra side, Jamie — we need to confirm VPC peering, private networking and KMS integration.
[01:42] Jamie: Right, also curious about KV cache behavior. Our chat sessions rely heavily on prefix caching to hit latency targets. If the cache changes behavior, tail latency goes up.
[01:50] Priya: Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching and we have configurable cache sizing and eviction policies. For Dedicated we can surface OS-level metrics and tracing. For Private we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit log forwarding.
[02:05] Carlos: What about quantization? We were experimenting with 4-bit quant profiles with vLLM to save cost. Can Redwood run those in Dedicated?
[02:12] Priya: Yes, we have quantized execution paths — we recommend a small matrix of experiments (fp16, int8, 4-bit) because quality tradeoffs vary by model. We also recommend running evals to capture any regression. Our Optimize tooling suggests quantization profiles by workload.
[02:28] Nina: Any limitations on model families? We use some Anthropic-style safety prompts and also occasionally call embeddings for search; we need consistent embedding similarity.
[02:35] Alex: We support a curated catalog — Open model variants, and Redwood-verified performance profiles. Embedding parity is part of the eval suite; sometimes we suggest an embedding model mapping. We'll share mapping docs.
[02:48] Sarah: Latency targets — p95 < 300ms for short chat messages (<=128 tokens), average gen latency ideally <150ms. Is that realistic on Dedicated?
[02:57] Priya: For that envelope yes, with Dedicated pools and right batching settings. We can size a reserved pool to hit throughput and latency SLOs. We'll verify with a perf run using your prompt set.
[03:08] Carlos: Cost question — how do dedicated commits compare to hosted per-token pricing? We need to see if it's worth moving.
[03:14] Alex: We provide reserved capacity commitments with monthly/annual pricing and burst options. For your volume (~50k reqs/day) the math often works out, especially once you factor in batching and prefix cache savings. I'll send a pricing spreadsheet with model SKU examples.
[03:27] Sarah: On the migration path — we also care about minimal change to code. Does Redwood expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint?
[03:33] Priya: We offer OpenAI-compatible routes for common generative calls, plus first-class SDKs. For specialized features like function calling, we have supported patterns but recommend testing.
[03:43] Jamie: What about fallback? If a dedicated pool is saturated, can we burst to hosted or another region?
[03:49] Priya: Yes, smart routing and graceful fallbacks are core — you can configure policies to route to hosted or a different model variant to keep live traffic flowing.
[03:58] Carlos: Security / compliance — SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC?
[04:02] Tomas: Tomas chiming in — we can share our security package; Dedicated and Private both support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations. For Private we can support on-prem or VPC with customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[04:15] Nina: Contracting timeline — we usually need procurement + legal review. Would a POC contract be possible?
[04:20] Alex: Yes, we do POC engagements, often with a limited dedicated pool and a perf run. We can scope a 4–6 week POC.
[04:28] Sarah: Great. For the perf run: our golden set is about 2000 prompts across chat & rerank. Throughput is about 50k/day with 3x peak. We'll share the set.
[04:36] Priya: Perfect — if you send the set, we'll run it under the same harness. We'll capture latency distributions, token counts, and quality deltas.
[04:45] Jamie: On infra, I want to confirm deployment automation — terraform? Helm?
[04:48] Priya: For Private we provide IaC modules: Terraform modules and Helm charts depending on deployment. For Dedicated, it's managed but we provide networking runbooks.
[04:57] Carlos: Any gotchas with TGI or vLLM pipelines we should be aware of?
[05:01] Priya: Two things: one, model artifacts and tokenizer differences — we validate tokenization. Two, runtime behaviors like sampling seeds or fallback randomness can cause small output drift. That's why we do utterance-level delta reports. For TGI pipelines specifically, if you rely heavily on custom logits processors, we map those behaviors and surface inconsistencies.
[05:21] Sarah: Ok sounds good. A couple of open concerns: 1) embeddings parity for semantic search; 2) rerank reproducibility; 3) cost modeling.
[05:29] Alex: We'll handle (1) by providing embedding model mappings and running the embedding recall tests. (2) We'll run rerank harness with your scoring function; if model differences exist we can recommend alternate model or prompt tuning. (3) I'll run cost scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[05:45] Nina: Timeline — if we commit to a POC, how long to stand up dedicated pool and run benchmarks?
[05:51] Alex: Typically 1–2 weeks to provision Dedicated (depending on capacity) and then 1–2 weeks for perf and eval. For Private it can be longer due to networking. We'll put a target on provisioning based on your region.
[06:02] Carlos: Any support commitments during POC?
[06:05] Tomas: We assign an SE and CSM during POC with scheduled touchpoints and a runbook for diagnostics.
[06:10] Sarah: Great, last Q: any examples of customers who moved from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated?
[06:14] Alex: Yes — we have a few case studies, happy to share anonymized numbers; they've seen 30–60% cost reduction on token costs after batching/caching and targeted quantization. We'll include sample dashboards.
[06:27] Carlos: Awesome.
[06:29] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll share pricing and capacity spreadsheet; Priya will schedule perf run pending sample prompts; Tomas will push security docs; Meridian will send prompt set and throughput numbers. Anything else?
[06:42] Sarah: No, that covers it. Thanks all.
[06:45] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email and set a concrete perf run date.

End of transcript.
